topics.title: Market for Ideas: Mokyr & the Enlightenment
Solow Model: Capital, Saving & Steady State

modes.title: Mock quiz
modes.blurb: The paper as announced: the 16-cell table, Mokyr, the Solow graph and the computers calculation.
modes.why: The quiz is 120 minutes with a calculator. Over a third is the 16-cell results table, worked from nothing but a demand curve and marginal cost. Under a third is multiple choice on Mokyr and the market for ideas. Then Solow graph questions (steady state, war casualties, what a policymaker's change does to the curves) and the company-level computers calculation. Game theory (mixed strategies) is not examined.

modes.title: Fill the table
modes.blurb: A fresh demand curve and MC: all 16 cells of the results table.
modes.why: Over a third of the quiz. Given only P = A − Q and MC, fill total output, price, Total Value (P × Q) and total profit for Bertrand, Stackelberg, Cournot and collusion. Outputs are A − C, ¾, ⅔ and ½ of it; everything else follows from demand.

modes.title: Solow graph
modes.blurb: Read the diagram: steady state, war casualties, policy shifts.
modes.why: The Solow block is multiple choice on the s·f(k) vs depreciation diagram: where k* is, which way k moves, what a war does, and which curve a policymaker's change moves.

modes.title: Computers
modes.blurb: The company-level Solow calculation with fresh rates.
modes.why: Depreciation, effective workers and computers to add: (δ + n + g) × N. New workers are not boosted by technology, which is why the rates add.

modes.title: Packet problems
modes.blurb: The packet's own numbers and pop-quiz questions.
modes.why: The quiz is written from this packet. These are its worked examples exactly as given: Grab and Uber at P = 339 − Q and pop-quiz questions Q1, Q3, Q4 and Q5. Know these cold before moving to fresh numbers.

modes.title: Explain it
modes.blurb: Why, not what: pick the reasoning a marker would accept.
modes.why: These give you the causal chain and its tempting wrong versions: level vs growth effect, why China had few ideas despite its audience, why a war on capital means fast growth and a war on workers means negative growth.

modes.title: Formula drill
modes.blurb: Each formula recalled, then used once.
modes.why: MR = a − 2Q, the reaction function, Δk = sf(k) − (δ + n + g)k, MPK = δ: if a formula is not instant, the calculation questions cost twice the time.

modes.title: Exam core
modes.blurb: The formula sheet and the ten traps, as questions.
modes.why: One pass over the highest-yield facts across all three blocks.
